## AIController

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/AIController.gd`, extends [`ControllerBase`](#controllerbase)

The AI's hands: turns what the AI's behaviours tell it into one InputCommand per tick.

A component of the pawn's AIManager (`AIManager.controller`); the ControllerManager puts it in charge whenever no player has the pawn. It decides nothing: the AI's behaviours (or a script or test) tell it what to do, and it builds the same input a player's controller makes. Everything it's told stays until changed, except `press()`, which lasts one tick. Until `look_at_point()` is called it keeps the pawn's own look. Its walks follow its own `path_follower`.

```gdscript
ai.move_to(point)                        # walks there along a nav path; false if there's no way there
ai.move_in_direction(Vector3(1, 0, 0))   # keeps walking that way; drops any path
ai.press(&"jump")                        # held for one tick, so the pawn sees one press
ai.follow(target, 1.2)                   # a persistent order: closes in on target until a move order (netcode spec 19.10)
```

A dead pawn's controller takes no orders, and lets go of everything as the pawn dies; the controllers README has the rest. Design: pawn spec 6.3, 10.3.

### Settings and properties

- `order_listener: Callable` = `Callable()`: Sees every order given to any AIController, in order: `order_listener.call(controller, order, args)`, order being the method's name (&"move_to", &"press"...). Empty by default. The order stream's tap (netcode spec 19.3): the same orders, at the same point of the same ticks, give the same input.
- `path_settings: PathFollowSettings`: How its walks follow their paths (closeness, nav tier, links, waiting for nav). Empty: the defaults.
- `path_follower: PathFollower` = `<unknown>`: The path its walks follow (move_to, follow, keep_distance), with `path_settings`.
- `look_from_height: float` = `1.3`: Where its look pitch is measured from: metres above the pawn's feet. Matches a ranged attack's muzzle_height (1.3), so a shot fired along the look meets the point looked at.

### Constants

- `_Follow.NONE = 0`
- `_Follow.CLOSE_IN = 1`
- `_Follow.KEEP_AWAY = 2`

### Functions

- `follow(node: Node3D, stop_distance: float, look_offset: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 1, 0), band: float = 0.3, repath_ticks: int = 20, repath_distance: float = 1.5) -> void`: Closes in on a node and stops stop_distance away (flat), looking at it offset above its origin; walks again once it's further than stop_distance plus band. Repaths every repath_ticks (at 60 a second) or when the node has moved repath_distance from where the path leads. Carried out at every input until a move order or another persistent order; a freed node ends it (standing still).
- `keep_distance(node: Node3D, distance: float, band: float = 1.5, look_offset: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 1, 0), repath_ticks: int = 20, repath_distance: float = 1.5) -> void`: Keeps about distance (flat) from a node, closing in when further and backing away when nearer, and stands, looking at it, once within band of that distance (half of it, from walking). Otherwise as `follow()`.
- `get_followed_node() -> Node3D`: The node a persistent order follows, or null.
- `is_standing_by() -> bool`: True while a persistent order has it standing (near enough, or at its distance).
- `move_to(point: Vector3) -> bool`: Walks to this point along a nav path, and stands still once there. Returns false (and stands still) if there's no way there. While not in charge it only remembers the point and returns true.
- `is_following_order() -> bool`: True while its own last move_to is under way: following its path (or waiting for nav, PENDING) when in charge, or waiting to start it when not. False once it arrives, gives up, or is told to do something else.
- `move_in_direction(direction: Vector3) -> void`: Walks this way, in world space, up to length 1, until told otherwise. Shorter is slower.
- `stop() -> void`: Stands still. Held actions stay held.
- `look_at_point(point: Vector3) -> void`: Looks at a point in the world. Does nothing without a pawn, since there's nowhere to look from.
- `look_at_node(node: Node3D, offset: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 0, 0)) -> void`: Keeps looking at a node, at offset from its origin, worked out again at every input, until `stop_looking()` or another look. For a behaviour that sleeps through a swing. A freed node ends it.
- `look_at_node_quietly(node: Node3D, offset: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 0, 0)) -> void`: The same as `look_at_node()` without counting as an order: for a persistent order, whose own order covers its look.
- `stop_looking() -> void`: Stops looking at anything in particular, and keeps whatever look the pawn already has.
- `is_looking_at_point() -> bool`: True while it's looking at a point it was given. AI sight faces this way then (SightSense).
- `press(action: StringName) -> void`: Holds this action for the next tick only, so the pawn sees one press.
- `hold(action: StringName, held: bool = true) -> void`: Holds or lets go of this action, until changed.
- `release_all() -> void`: Back to idle: standing still, nothing held. The look direction stays.
- `take_input_command(_tick: int) -> InputCommand`: This tick's input. Uses up press(), so call it once per tick: ControllerManager does.
- `let_go() -> void`: Forgets every order (standing, nothing held, no look, no persistent order), without counting as one. The pawn calls it through its ControllerManager on each tick it's dead, on every machine that runs it, so it comes back from a revive with no orders and gives none while dead (netcode spec 19.10).
- `get_path_follower() -> PathFollower`: Its `path_follower` while a walk is under way, else null.
- `drop_path() -> void`: Drops the path it's following. A walk given while it wasn't in charge is kept, and starts when it's in charge again.

## ControllerBase

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/ControllerBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The base class every controller shares: PlayerController and AIController extend it.

Pawn spec section 6. A controller decides nothing about how a pawn moves. Its only output is one InputCommand per tick, and the pawn's abilities do the rest. That's why a player and the AI can take turns driving the same pawn.

How to make one: extend this, and override `take_input_command()`.

### Settings and properties

- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this controller drives, or null.

### Signals

- `pawn_changed(pawn: Pawn)`

### Functions

- `take_input_command(_tick: int) -> InputCommand`: This tick's input. Called once per tick. The default is an idle command: standing still, nothing held.
- `get_path_follower() -> PathFollower`: The path follower its input walks the pawn along now, or null: none by default. CrowdMover asks the controller in charge, through `ControllerManager.get_path_follower()`, whether the pawn is crossing a nav link.
- `drop_path() -> void`: Drops any path it's walking the pawn along. The ControllerManager calls it when someone else takes charge, so nobody walks the rest of another's path once charge comes back. Nothing by default.

## ControllerManager

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/ControllerManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Picks whose input a pawn follows, and holds that input and whether a player has the pawn.

A part on the pawn, added by PawnInitializer. This machine's player controller is in charge when it has the pawn; nobody is when a player elsewhere has it (the input arrives over the network); otherwise the AI's controller is (`ai_controller`, from the AIManager), so it takes over the moment a player lets go. The pawn calls `tick_input()` once per tick, which asks the controller in charge and writes its command into the input; controllers never write to the pawn themselves. While the pawn owns a tag `input_blocked_by` matches (status.dead by default), or nobody here is in charge, the input is cleared (pawn spec 16.4).

The input rolls back (the pawn's TickStateComponent lists it, with `previous_held_actions` as state). The server's checks on a client's input are here too (`sanitize_network_input()`), as the NetworkEntity's input_owner. Only PlayerController calls `attach_player()` and `detach_player()`. Use `get_controller_in_charge()` (a ControllerBase, or null) and `was_action_pressed(&"jump")` (held this tick, not last tick). Design: pawn spec 6.4, 8.17, 16.4.

### Settings and properties

- `possessable: bool` = `true`: Whether a player may take control of this pawn. Turn it off on pawns players should never control. To change it where the ControllerManager comes from the game's defaults, add parts/ControllerManager.tscn to the pawn scene first.
- `input_blocked_by: TagQuery` = `<unknown>`: While the pawn owns tags this matches, its input is cleared (nothing held, no direction; the look stays), whoever is in charge: the pattern of Unreal GAS's blocking tags. By default any of status.dead; add status.stunned or a cutscene's tag. Empty: never blocked.
- `missing_input_hold_ticks: int` = `-1`: On the server: when a client's input goes missing, the last one repeats in full for this many ticks. -1 uses NetworkSession's setting of the same name, which is the game-wide rule. Set a number only for a pawn that needs its own.
- `missing_input_fade_ticks: int` = `-1`: Then its direction fades to nothing over this many ticks. -1 uses NetworkSession's setting.
- `move_input: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: the direction to go, in world space, up to length 1
- `held_actions: int` = `0`: which named actions are held this tick, as bits from InputActions
- `look_yaw: float` = `0.0`: where the player is looking, which is often not where the pawn is facing
- `look_pitch: float` = `0.0`: where the player is looking, up and down
- `view_ticks_behind: float` = `0.0`: How many ticks behind its own tick the controller was drawing other pawns, for lag compensation. The server limits it to what's believable (LagCompensation).
- `previous_held_actions: int` = `0`: Last tick's held_actions, so a press can be told from a hold. In the TickState's state list, so a correction fixes it.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this manager belongs to, or null if its parent isn't one.
- `ai_controller: ControllerBase`: The AI's controller, from the pawn's AIManager (`AIManager.controller`). Null if the pawn has no AI or its AI has none.
- `player_controller: ControllerBase` = `null`: This machine's player controller while it has the pawn, or null.

### Signals

- `controller_changed(controller: ControllerBase)`: Sent when a different controller is in charge, or none. The controller is null when nobody here is. It's sent at the end of the frame, once, with the final answer: possessing takes two steps (a player has it, then their controller attaches), and listeners shouldn't see "nobody" in between.
- `possession_changed(pawn: Pawn, has_player: bool)`: Sent when a player takes this pawn, or lets it go.

### Functions

- `get_controller_in_charge() -> ControllerBase`: Who the pawn follows right now, or null. See the rule in the class description.
- `get_path_follower() -> PathFollower`: The path follower the controller in charge walks the pawn along now, or null (pawn spec 16.7).
- `take_input_command(tick: int) -> InputCommand`: This tick's input from the controller in charge, or null when nobody here is.
- `tick_input(tick: int) -> void`: The pawn calls this once per tick, in its input phase: asks the controller in charge and writes its command into the input. It's cleared instead while blocked (`input_blocked_by`), on every machine, and with nobody in charge (no controller here, no player elsewhere). A script that writes input later in the same phase wins.
- `is_input_blocked() -> bool`: True while the pawn owns a tag `input_blocked_by` matches, such as status.dead.
- `apply_input(command: InputCommand) -> void`: Writes a command into this tick's input.
- `is_action_held(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if a named action is held this tick.
- `was_action_pressed(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if a named action is held this tick but wasn't last tick: a press.
- `clear_input() -> void`: Nothing pressed, no direction. Keeps where it looks. Done while the input is blocked, with nobody in charge, and when a player lets go.
- `finish_tick() -> void`: Once this tick's input has been read: what was held, so the next tick can tell a press from a hold; and a tick with real input ends a run of missing ones. The pawn calls this in its simulate step, after its abilities, before it moves.
- `decides_own_input() -> bool`: True where this pawn's input is decided: offline, its owner's machine, or the server for a pawn nobody owns. False on the server for a client's pawn, whose input arrives over the network, and on a client for anyone else's pawn.
- `has_player() -> bool`: True if a player controls this pawn. On a client, that's any player, not only this machine's.
- `set_has_player(value: bool) -> void`: PossessionCoordinator tells the pawn's manager. Nothing else should call this.
- `sanitize_network_input(values: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: On the server: a client's input is never trusted. Wrong types are replaced and direction is limited to full speed. Keys are as the pawn's TickState lists them ("ControllerManager:move_input"); plain names work too.
- `_network_input_missing() -> void`: On the server: this tick's input never arrived, so the last one repeats (a held direction repeats; a press doesn't). After missing_input_hold_ticks the direction fades out over missing_input_fade_ticks. Held actions are left alone.
- `attach_player(controller: ControllerBase) -> void`: PlayerController calls this when it takes the pawn.
- `detach_player(controller: ControllerBase) -> void`: PlayerController calls this when it lets go. A controller that isn't the attached one changes nothing.
- `_refresh() -> void`: Checks at the end of the frame whether who's in charge changed. Several changes in one frame give one check.

## ControllerStepHost

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/ControllerStepHost.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Runs steps that write a controller's input, such as the player's click-to-move ([`MoveToStep`](../steps/REFERENCE.md#movetostep)): a small step host (pawn spec 16.4).

A child of its controller, with its steps as its own children. It owns a [`StepTimeline`](../steps/REFERENCE.md#steptimeline) whose entries are all manual: nothing starts until `start()` does, and one start ends any run before it. Each tick its controller calls `run()`, which clears `input` and lets the running steps write it; the controller then uses what they wrote. It runs on the controller's machine only, so nothing here rolls back: the input it makes does.

```gdscript
host.start(host.get_node(^"MoveTo"))   # begins a run with this step
host.run(pawn.ticks_elapsed)           # once per tick, while is_running()
```

### Settings and properties

- `input: InputCommand` = `<unknown>`: What the running steps wrote this tick: move, and actions to press. Look is left to the controller.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn its steps move. `set_pawn()` changes it.
- `timeline: StepTimeline` = `<unknown>`: The timeline its steps run on, built when it's ready.

### Functions

- `set_pawn(new_pawn: Pawn) -> void`: Moves its steps to this pawn (null: none), ending any run, since its steps belonged to the last one.
- `start(step: Step) -> bool`: Ends any run, then begins one with this step, which enters at once. False if it isn't one of this host's steps or there's no pawn.
- `run(elapsed: int = 1) -> void`: Runs the running steps for this tick, covering elapsed ticks, after clearing `input`. The run ends once no step is left.
- `step_input() -> InputCommand`: The input its steps write (`input`): how a [`MoveStep`](../steps/REFERENCE.md#movestep) finds it when the timeline is built.
- `stop() -> void`: Ends the run, stopping every running step ("cancelled").
- `is_running() -> bool`: True while a run is going.

## InputActions

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/InputActions.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Turns action names like &"jump" into bits, so an input command carries every held action in one int.

One int is much smaller than a list of names on the network, and "is jump held?" is one AND. Every machine must give an action the same bit, so the game lists its actions in resources/input_actions.tres (an InputActionsRes) and each gets the bit of its place in the list; the list is part of NetworkSession's content hash. An unlisted action is added with a warning offline, and gets no bit (never held) in a network session. Past 64 actions the extras get no bit.

A static class, not an autoload, so it works in headless tests. Design: pawn spec 5.

### Constants

- `MAX_ACTIONS = 64`
- `LIST_PATH = "res://assets/scripts/resources/input_actions.tres"`

### Functions

- `mask_of(action: StringName) -> int` *(static)*: The mask with this action's bit, or 0 for a blank name.
- `mask_of_list(actions: Array) -> int` *(static)*: The mask with all these actions' bits.
- `all_listed_mask() -> int` *(static)*: Every listed action's bit. The server uses it to throw away bits a client made up.
- `names_in(mask: int) -> StringName[]` *(static)*: The names of the actions in a mask, for debug readouts.
- `get_actions() -> StringName[]` *(static)*: Every action, in bit order.
- `reset() -> void` *(static)*: Forgets everything, so the next use reads the list again. For tests.
- `use_list(actions: Array) -> void` *(static)*: Uses this list instead of the file. For tests.
- `_is_online() -> bool` *(static)*: True while this machine is a server or a client. A static class has no node of its own, so it asks the tree.

## InputCommand

`res://assets/scripts/controllers/InputCommand.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

One tick's input for a pawn, as plain values: what players and AI both make, and what goes over the network.

Pawn spec section 5. Nothing holds what a pawn wants between ticks except the last input: there's no "intent".

How to use it: a controller makes one each tick, and the pawn's ControllerManager copies it into the pawn's input (`ControllerManager.apply_input()`). In a script or test, this is the short way:

```gdscript
InputCommand.make(direction, [&"sprint"])
```

### Settings and properties

- `move: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: Which way to go, in world space, up to length 1. Shorter means slower, as a stick pushed halfway gives.
- `look_yaw: float` = `0.0`: Where the controller is looking, sideways, in radians. Often not where the pawn faces.
- `look_pitch: float` = `0.0`: Where the controller is looking, up and down, in radians.
- `held_actions: int` = `0`: Which named actions are held this tick, as bits from InputActions. A press is "held this tick, not held last tick", which the ControllerManager works out, so a press is never sent twice.
- `view_ticks_behind: float` = `0.0`: How many ticks behind its own tick the sender was drawing other pawns, for lag compensation. The player's controller fills it from NetworkSession; the AI's stays 0.

### Functions

- `make(move_direction: Vector3 = Vector3(0, 0, 0), held: Array = [], yaw: float = 0.0, pitch: float = 0.0) -> InputCommand` *(static)*: A command in one line. held is a list of action names, such as `[&"jump", &"sprint"]`.
- `is_held(action: StringName) -> bool`
- `set_held(action: StringName, held: bool = true) -> void`
